# Canonical lockstep atan2 edge vectors (ADR-8876, MATH_BITS_VERSION 1). One row per input pair:
# "Y X R", the binary32 bits of y, x and the expected math::atan2(y, x), in hex.
# Inputs: every pair of 26 edge values (+-0, +-inf, quiet/signaling NaNs with payloads and signs, +-1,
# the smallest subnormals, the smallest normals, the largest finites, tiny and huge ratios) plus 14
# hand-picked pairs (near the diagonal, the axes, extreme ratios, an underflowing negative result).
# R comes from an independent decimal-arithmetic oracle (80 digits: argument halving and a Taylor series,
# exact round-to-nearest-even to binary32, subnormals included) with the canonical policy applied:
# signed-zero inputs as +0, any NaN input -> 7fc00000, a zero result is +0, IEEE 754 section 9.2.1 values for
# infinities. Regenerate only with a MATH_BITS_VERSION bump; never by running math::atan2.
